Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

A window over wider content moves with time: scroll, marquee and slide (rich-animation-42lg.re8)

scroll(content, { width, height, col, row }) is an Animation<Renderable>
of a fixed slot over content drawn at its natural size, each offset an
Animation<number>. frameAt now draws any renderable's animation with its
cells stamped at the host's time.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

An element enters, stays, leaves, and the host knows when it is gone (rich-animation-42lg.588) (#487)

* An element enters, stays, leaves, and the host knows when it is gone (rich-animation-42lg.588)

lifecycle(element, { enter, exit, key, theme }, entered) is an Animation<Renderable> on the host's clock; leave(at) tells it to leave and gone(t) says when to drop it. Every boundary is read through the transition's own done, carried onto host time by firstReaching. Transition gains seconds.

* A lifecycle's frame says when it changes even with no cells; Transition loses seconds (rich-animation-42lg.588)

Before it entered the frame had no cell to carry its stamp, so a function view never woke to show it arrive; the stamp now also rides a zero-width cell. doneAt searches from the start, so Transition no longer carries a seconds that could disagree with done.
